concept: Everything here is glass. A photoreal pastel-glass world is introduced in silence, a steel ball rolls in (Aim. Fire.), and on the music's drop it smashes the glass in ultra slow motion. The shards become the game: SHARD on a floating phone, then a beat-cut montage where each real level rhymes with the same world made real (dawn towers in a chain reaction, ember blasts, night pendants falling through a moonbeam), the five worlds, the twelve balls, a one-cut-per-beat climax, the shatter rewinding in the break, and the logo landing on the second drop.
logline: The glass game, made real, then put in your pocket.

output_target.audio: Take this Higher (Mixkit asset 1012) from 0 to 32.9 s at its own 124 BPM; recorded SFX; master about -12.5 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP

look: photoreal generated worlds in the game's pastel glass palettes (sky blue #96CDFF, blush #FFBEC8, lilac #BEAFFF; Dawn peach, Ember coral, Night navy) + clean Apple-like motion graphics in Nunito 900/800
beat: t(b) = b * 0.48388 s (124 BPM, downbeats every 4 beats; drop b16 = 7.74 s, break b56.5 = 27.34 s, second drop b60 = 29.03 s, end b68 = 32.90 s)

setup: the steel ball at rest, then rolling and accelerating toward the tallest tower
climax 1, the wow: impact on the drop, ultra slow-motion shatter toward camera; SHARD wordmark assembles among the shards at b20

hero: The game itself. The steel ball appears in generated shots described in text: the game's 2D ball render has a stylised curved rim highlight that a photoreal model would copy as a painted stripe, so it is not sent as a reference.
sound_plan: Music: 'Take this Higher' by Michael Ramir C. (Mixkit Stock Music Free License) from 0 s, fading over the last bar to 32.9 s. SFX: the game's own glass, cannon and bomb recordings, Katana's CC0 library (hits, whooshes, risers) and the Pixabay library effects already licensed in this project; aligned to impacts, type slams and cuts.
energy: Authored, no reference: a near-still, silent opening; accelerating build; a hard impact with flash and shake on the drop; one cut per bar in the montage, one per beat in the climax; a slow rewind in the break; a single slam on the second drop.
